title: Input and Pesticide Compliance: Verify Before Use

content.overview: Input compliance is a verification workflow. Before any pesticide or other regulated cultivation input is used, the learner must identify the exact product, open the current label and hazard information, verify the intended crop/site/use, determine which worker-protection and access requirements apply, check jurisdiction-specific restrictions, and preserve a traceable record of the decision. Marketing terms such as natural, organic or commonly used do not establish authorization.

vocabulary.definition: The crop, site, rate, method and other conditions directed or authorized by the product label and applicable law.
Entry into a treated area after application, subject to applicable label, worker-protection and jurisdictional restrictions.
A traceable record linking a product and label/version to date, location, crop/site, use, amount, operator and required safety or access information.
A missing, conflicting or unclear requirement that prevents the learner from concluding that the proposed use may proceed.
The current official label, regulation, agency guidance, license condition or other authoritative source used to support a compliance decision.

sections.title: Verify the exact product and current label
sections.body: A recommendation is not enough. Confirm the product identity and current label/version before relying on rate, crop/site, PPE, reentry, disposal or other directions. Preserve the source or version used so the decision can be reconstructed later.

sections.title: Crop, site and use are separate checks
sections.body: A product that is lawful in one context may not be allowed for every crop, location, production system or application method. The verification record should state the intended crop/site/use explicitly rather than assuming general agricultural availability means universal authorization.

sections.title: Worker protection is part of compliance
sections.body: Where applicable, worker and handler protections include training, application information, labeling access, PPE, notification, restricted-entry controls, decontamination and emergency assistance. The learner must determine which protections actually apply to the operation and task instead of treating them as optional add-ons.

sections.title: Jurisdiction can add or change requirements
sections.body: Federal guidance does not eliminate state, tribal, local, license or facility requirements. If the applicable authority is unclear, the correct response is to document the gap and escalate before use rather than selecting the least restrictive interpretation.

sections.title: Records preserve the compliance decision
sections.body: A strong application or pre-use record preserves the product, label/version, date, location, crop/site, intended use, responsible person, safety controls, access/reentry information and source used for authorization. Keeping this evidence supports worker communication, audits, corrective action and future review.

workedExamples: A product marketed as natural is recommended for a cannabis crop. The team still verifies the exact label, intended crop/site/use and applicable jurisdiction before deciding whether it can be used.
A label used last season has changed. The current application record stores the new label/version instead of assuming last year's directions still apply.
A worker-protection requirement applies to the planned task, but required decontamination supplies are not ready. The task does not proceed until the requirement is satisfied.
Two official sources appear to conflict about a restriction. The learner documents the conflict and escalates it rather than choosing the more convenient interpretation.
commonMistakes: Assuming natural, organic or commonly used means unrestricted.
Using a screenshot or old label instead of the current product source.
Checking rate but not crop, site, method or worker-protection requirements.
Treating PPE as proof that an otherwise unauthorized use is acceptable.
Failing to retain enough source/version detail to reconstruct why a use was approved.
content.practicalApplication: Create a complete pre-use verification record for a supplied training product or approved supervised example. Record exact product identity, current label/version, crop/site/use, jurisdiction/source checked, PPE, worker communication, decontamination, access/reentry, emergency information, required application records and any unresolved authorization gap. The exercise ends in either a documented proceed decision supported by the supplied sources or a documented stop-and-escalate decision.
content.summary: Responsible input use depends on evidence, not familiarity. Product identity, current label, crop/site/use, worker protection, jurisdiction, access controls and traceable records must agree before a proposed application is treated as acceptable.

blocks.title: Pre-use compliance matrix
rows: Intended use is absent, prohibited or unclear
Controlling authority or restriction is unresolved
Record cannot show why the decision was made

blocks.title: Natural does not mean unrestricted
blocks.setting: A pest-control product is advertised as natural and widely recommended by growers. The current label and jurisdictional use have not been checked.
options: Use it because natural products are exempt from restrictions
Use a reduced rate until approval is confirmed
Stop and verify the current label, crop/site/use, worker protections and jurisdiction before application
blocks.answer: Stop and verify the current label, crop/site/use, worker protections and jurisdiction before application.
blocks.feedback: Marketing language and community use do not establish legal or safe use in the intended context.

blocks.title: Complete a pre-use authorization record
blocks.instructions: Use a supplied training label, SDS and jurisdiction packet. Do not conduct a real application unless separately authorized and supervised.
prompts: Record the exact product and label/version.
State the crop, site and intended use.
List the worker-protection controls that apply.
State whether authorization is complete or whether the task must stop and escalate.

blocks.title: No implied authorization
blocks.body: THC Academy training does not authorize pesticide application or other regulated input use. Real work must follow the current label, employer program and all applicable jurisdictional requirements.

visualNeeds.teachingObjective: Learner connects product identity, label, SDS, crop/site/use, worker protection and jurisdiction to one go/no-go decision.
Learner sees which fields preserve traceability and safe access decisions.
